kurz: Large holes need three things: a stretchy network, enough gas and a dough soft enough to expand.
bild_im_kopf: Like bubble gum bubbles: with soft, stretchy gum they get big; with hard gum they stay small.
bedeutung: Holes are gas bubbles that the [[glutenbildung|gluten network]] holds in place in the oven. More water in the dough makes the network stretchier, a long prove brings more gas and gentle shaping preserves the bubbles.
was_passiert: A soft, wet dough lets bubbles grow large. Stretching and folding strengthens the network without crushing the bubbles. [[dampf-im-ofen|Steam in the oven]] keeps the crust soft so the loaf can still rise.
faustregeln: More water in the dough, but only as much as you can handle.
Do not knock out the gas when shaping; build tension gently.

praxis.text: Ciabatta and sourdough with a lot of water, sandwich bread with little: the amount of water decides the crumb.
